main_text.p: sentire, & ab Hebræo Judaico dissentire v. 28.cap. 12. Deut. ita legunt 70. Φυλαξον ἡ ἀκουε ἡ ποιήσεις, &c. in Hebræo abest ἡ ποιήσεις; sed illud repræsentant uterque Samaritanus. In fine ejusdem versus LXX. τὸ ἀρεστὸν ἡ τὸ καλὸν Hebræi legunt ordine inverso [illegible, ~5 letters] καλὸν ἡ ἀρεστὸν uterq; Samaritanus bonum & placitum, Ver. 32. Hebræi legunt præcipio vobis, uterque Samaritanus præcipio hodie, 70. verò utramque lectionem jungunt, ἐντέλλομαί ὑμῖν σήμερον, hæc tantum ex schedula tua observata sunto: nam plurima ejusdem generis, ex continua Pentateuchi istius lectione mihi præsto sunt, quæ Epistolii modum longè excedunt; plurima denique ex eodem codice, quæ masoreticas censuras, λεπτολογίας, superstitiosa & ridicula mysteria plane evertunt. Avide legi, quæ de Samaritanis scripsisti; non existimabam, gentem illam ad tantam paucitatem redactam esse: miror quomodo in tam contemnenda paucitate librum legis, & cæremonias suas conservare potuerunt.

page.notes: The Hebrew phrase after "ordine inverso" on the line of Deut. 12 is too faint to read letter by letter and is marked illegible. The Greek forms are read as best possible; the accents and breathings in the Greek of "Φυλαξον" and "ἀκουε" are doubtful. The running head is in small capitals. The page number is read as 182. The left margin carries only stains and show-through; there are no notes.
